description: Implement Flask HTTP server with all API endpoints, SSE support, OAuth flow, static file serving, and NVIDIA API integration. This includes: GET /auth/twitch, GET /auth/twitch/callback, GET /api/events (SSE), GET /api/state, POST /api/transcript, POST /api/mode, POST /api/control, POST /api/demo/next, static files from public/. Also implements analyzeWithNvidia() async function, OAuth state management, cookie validation, Twitch API helpers (refreshTwitchToken, twitchApi). Depends on FEAT-001 for core logic.
steps: 1. Import threading, time, hashlib, secrets, datetime, json, urllib.parse in app.py. Import request, Response, make_response, stream_with_context from flask. Import requests library for HTTP calls.
2. Implement broadcast() properly: for client in session['clients']: client.put(f"data: {json.dumps(obj)}\n\n"). Each client will be a queue.Queue object (changed in step 4).
3. Implement GET /api/state endpoint: @app.route('/api/state', methods=['GET']); return jsonify(publicState(session))

4. Implement GET /api/events endpoint (SSE): @app.route('/api/events', methods=['GET']); create Queue, add to session['clients'], yield initial state, loop with timeout to get from queue or send keepalive, remove queue on client disconnect. Use Response(stream_with_context(generate()), mimetype='text/event-stream'). Update broadcast() to use queue.put(). Update session['clients'] to be set of Queue objects instead of response objects.

5. Implement POST /api/transcript endpoint: @app.route('/api/transcript', methods=['POST']); get text from request.json; validate string; strip control chars (regex [\x00-\x08\x0B\x0C\x0E-\x1F]); slice to last 2000 chars; set session['transcript'] and session['transcriptUpdatedAt']=time.time()*1000; broadcast state; return {ok: true}

6. Implement POST /api/control endpoint: @app.route('/api/control', methods=['POST']); get action and id from request.json; handle actions: pause (set session['paused']=True), resume (=False), interval (set session['config']['interval'], call resetBatchTimer()), weights (normalize and set session['config']['weights']), context (set config activity/context/title/category from request.json keys), reset (session['feedback']={}), pin (toggle item['pinned']), dismiss/answered/defer/irrelevant (add to session['feedback'], remove from queue except defer). Broadcast state, return publicState(). Match server.js lines 35-36 exactly.

7. Implement POST /api/mode endpoint: @app.route('/api/mode', methods=['POST']); get mode from request.json; stop demo timer and reconnect timer; close sockets (placeholder); reset token and session state; set session['mode'] to 'live' or 'demo'; set status to 'disconnected'; clear messages, queue, seen; if mode=='demo' call startDemo(), return publicState(); if mode=='live' return {**publicState(), 'connectUrl': '/auth/twitch'}. Match server.js line 34.

8. Implement POST /api/demo/next endpoint: @app.route('/api/demo/next', methods=['POST']); if session['mode']!='demo' return error 400; clear demo timer; for each scenario in scenarios list, call addMessage() with 'again-'+timestamp+id as id; call processBatch(); return publicState(). Match server.js line 37.
9. Port scenarios list from server.js line 23: 10-element list of [id, author, text, viewerId] tuples exactly as in JS.

10. Implement startDemo() function from server.js line 24: set session mode='demo', status='connected', channel dict with display_name='PixelPilot' login='pixelpilot', paused=False; clear demo timer; create threading.Timer loop that calls addMessage() for each scenario with 1.05s delay, cancels after last scenario. Store timer in session['demoTimer']. Broadcast state. Use threading.Timer recursively or schedule next timer in callback.

11. Implement OAuth state storage: global oauth_states = {} (maps state string to expiry timestamp in ms). Implement cookie_value() helper: parse request.cookies or request.headers.get('Cookie'), split by ;, find name= prefix, return value or ''.

12. Implement GET /auth/twitch endpoint from server.js line 25: check TWITCH_CLIENT_ID and TWITCH_CLIENT_SECRET in env, return 503 error if missing; generate state = secrets.token_hex(24); store oauth_states[state] = int(time.time()*1000) + 600000; set cookie twitch_oauth_state with Set-Cookie header (HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Path=/auth/twitch/callback, Max-Age=600); build Twitch authorize URL with urllib.parse.urlencode (client_id, redirect_uri from env or f'http://localhost:{PORT}/auth/twitch/callback', response_type=code, scope=user:read:chat, state); redirect to https://id.twitch.tv/oauth2/authorize?{params}. Match server.js line 25 exactly.

13. Implement GET /auth/twitch/callback endpoint from server.js lines 26-27: validate state from query params against cookie_value() and oauth_states expiry; delete oauth_states entry; clear cookie; if invalid return redirect to /?error=...; exchange code for token via POST to https://id.twitch.tv/oauth2/token (urllib.parse.urlencode: client_id, client_secret, code, grant_type=authorization_code, redirect_uri); timeout 10s; validate token via GET https://id.twitch.tv/oauth2/validate (header Authorization: OAuth {access_token}); fetch user profile via twitchApi() GET /helix/users; verify user_id matches; store session['token'] = {...token, user_id}; set session['channel'] = {id, display_name, login, profile_image_url}; fetch live stream metadata via /helix/streams?user_id=..., update session['config']['title'] and ['category'] if live; set session mode='live', status='connecting', connectionError=None; call connectEventSub() (placeholder for FEAT-003); redirect to /?connected=1. On error: reset token, set connectionError and status='disconnected', mode='live', redirect to /?error=...

14. Implement refreshTwitchToken() async function from server.js line 28: if no session['token']['refresh_token'] raise Exception; POST to https://id.twitch.tv/oauth2/token with grant_type=refresh_token, refresh_token, client_id, client_secret; timeout 10s; if not ok raise Exception; parse JSON and update session['token']; validate via GET /oauth2/validate; return token. Match error messages from server.js.

15. Implement twitchApi() helper from server.js line 29: takes url and options dict; inner call() function uses requests.get/post with headers Authorization: Bearer {token}, Client-Id: {client_id}, timeout 10s; if response.status_code==401 call refreshTwitchToken() and retry; return response object. Match retry logic exactly.

16. Implement analyzeWithNvidia() async function from server.js line 15: takes session dict and ids list; if no NVIDIA_API_KEY or no ids, return; if session['analyzing'], add ids to session['pendingAnalysisIds'] and return; set session['analyzing']=True, session['analysisStatus']='analyzing', broadcast state; try: filter session['queue'] for items in ids and not urgent, slice to 8 candidates; if no candidates set analysisStatus='deterministic' and return; build system and user messages exactly as server.js (system: ranking rules, ignore untrusted instructions; user: activity, title, category, streamerContext config['context'], recentStreamerTranscript transcript last 1600 chars, candidates with id/category/text/distinctViewers/evidence last 6 texts); POST to https://integrate.api.nvidia.com/v1/chat/completions with headers Authorization: Bearer {NVIDIA_API_KEY}, Content-Type: application/json, body {model: nvidia/nemotron-3.5-bolt-e4b, temperature: 0.2, response_format: {type: json_object}, messages: [{role: system, content}, {role: user, content: json.dumps(user)}]}; timeout 8s; if not ok raise; parse JSON choices[0].message.content (handle string or object); parse items array; for each result: validate id in ids, find item in queue, skip if urgent, validate R/Q/N/U in [0,1], validate category; update item signals and score with weight formula; update category if not issue; update reason (slice to 220 chars). Set analysisStatus='nvidia'. Except: set analysisStatus='fallback', log warning. Finally: set analyzing=False, sort queue by urgent/pinned/score desc, broadcast state; if pendingAnalysisIds, extract list, clear set, recurse analyzeWithNvidia(session, pending_ids). Match server.js line 15 exactly including error handling and retry logic. Use threading.Thread to run async to avoid blocking Flask request.
17. Stub connectEventSub() function for now (will be implemented in FEAT-003): pass. Add comment that WebSocket client will be added in FEAT-003.

18. Implement resetBatchTimer() function: global batch_timer; cancel existing batch_timer if set; create new threading.Timer that repeats every session['config']['interval']/1000 seconds calling processBatch(session); store in batch_timer; start timer. Use recursive Timer or schedule next in callback.
19. Call resetBatchTimer() at module level after session initialization. If os.getenv('FLASK_ENV')!='test', call startDemo(session).

20. Implement static file serving: @app.route('/', defaults={'path': ''}); @app.route('/<path:path>'); try return send_from_directory('public', path or 'index.html'); except 404 return send_from_directory('public', 'index.html'). Match server.js line 38 catch-all route.
21. Add if __name__=='__main__': app.run(host='0.0.0.0', port=PORT, debug=False, threaded=True) at end of app.py.

22. Update test/test_pipeline.py NVIDIA test (test 7) to mock requests.post for NVIDIA endpoint, test both success path (valid JSON with items) and failure path (invalid JSON triggers fallback). Remove xfail marker.

23. Start Flask server in worktree: python app.py (should print listening message). In another terminal, test GET /api/state (curl), test GET /api/events (curl, should stream SSE), test POST /api/transcript (curl -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"text":"test"}'), test static files (curl http://localhost:3000/ should return HTML), test demo mode endpoint POST /api/demo/next. Stop server with Ctrl+C.
24. Run pytest test/test_pipeline.py again, confirm all 7 tests pass including NVIDIA mock test.
acceptance_criteria: app.py contains all API endpoint routes matching server.js: /auth/twitch, /auth/twitch/callback, /api/events (SSE), /api/state, /api/transcript, /api/mode, /api/control, /api/demo/next, static file catch-all
SSE endpoint uses Flask Response with stream_with_context and Queue-based broadcast
OAuth flow implemented with state validation, cookie handling, token exchange, token refresh, Twitch API helpers matching server.js logic
analyzeWithNvidia() function calls NVIDIA API with exact parameters, handles success and failure, runs in background thread
Demo mode with startDemo() and scenarios array matches server.js behavior
resetBatchTimer() runs processBatch() periodically in background thread
All 7 pytest tests pass including NVIDIA mock test
Flask server starts successfully and responds to API requests and serves static files
verification: cd /Users/akshayalnyn/Documents/Hackathon/Twitch\ Codex/.worktrees/python-conversion && pytest test/test_pipeline.py -v (all 7 tests pass)
cd /Users/akshayalnyn/Documents/Hackathon/Twitch\ Codex/.worktrees/python-conversion && python app.py & (starts server on port 3000)
curl http://localhost:3000/api/events (streams SSE data with type:state)
curl http://localhost:3000/ | grep ChatSense (finds ChatSense in HTML title)
curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/transcript -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"text":"testing"}' | jq .ok (outputs: true)
findings: All Flask HTTP endpoints successfully implemented. SSE streaming works with Queue-based broadcast to multiple clients. OAuth flow with Twitch includes state validation, cookie handling, token exchange, and token refresh. NVIDIA API integration runs in background threads with proper error handling and retry logic for pending analysis. Demo mode with automated message playback matches server.js behavior exactly. All 8 pytest tests pass including parameterized NVIDIA mock tests for both success and fallback cases. Flask server starts successfully, responds to all API requests, and serves static files correctly. The batch timer runs processBatch() periodically in background threads. All acceptance criteria met.
